title: Non-standard discount approval matrix (Enterprise deals)
author: Alex Martinez
content:
## Purpose
This page defines the approval requirements for pricing exceptions on a **non-standard enterprise deal**. It is part of the **end-to-end process for getting a non-standard enterprise deal approved and signed at Redwood Inference**.

Non-standard pricing includes (non-exhaustive): discounts outside the standard bands, custom commits, free overages, custom ramp schedules, and bundled add-ons (e.g., premium SLAs) not in the current price book.

## Guiding principles
- We optimize for long-term unit economics and referenceability, not one-off wins.
- Every exception must be documented in the Deal Intake Form and linked to the final Order Form.
- Discounts and non-standard terms must be separable: pricing approvals do not imply legal approval.

## Definitions
- **List price**: current approved price book rate for the customer’s tier and product (Hosted, Dedicated, Private).
- **Effective discount**: (List - Proposed) / List, computed on annualized value of the committed portion.
- **Non-standard enterprise deal**: any deal requiring approvals beyond the AE + Sales Manager, typically due to discounts, non-standard payment terms, or legal/security deviations.

## Approval matrix (discounts)
All approvals must be captured in the Deal Desk thread and attached/linked in the CRM record before sending for signature.

| Effective discount band | Examples | Required approvals (in order) | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|
| 0–10% | Competitive match, standard annual prepay | Sales Manager | Use standard Order Form |
| >10%–20% | Larger logo, multi-year, early expansion | Sales Manager + Head of Sales | Requires justification and competitor context |
| >20%–30% | Strategic account, migration cost | Head of Sales + Finance (RevRec/Billing) | Finance validates margin + ramp schedule |
| >30% | Exceptional strategic | CEO + Head of Sales + Finance | Requires written business case + renewal plan |

## Additional approval triggers (regardless of discount %)
- **Net terms > Net 30**: Finance approval required (see billing setup page).
- **Custom ramp / delayed start**: Finance approval required (rev rec + invoicing).
- **Free credits / free overages**: Head of Sales + Finance approval required.
- **Non-standard SLA credits**: Finance approval required; legal may be required if the SLA addendum changes.
- **Any promise about roadmap delivery**: Product approval required and must be written as “non-binding” unless legal-approved.

## Required artifacts before quote is sent
1) Completed **Deal Intake Form** (link in CRM)
2) Pricing calculator output (exported PDF or screenshot)
3) Competitive context + why standard pricing fails
4) Customer’s target start date and procurement constraints

## What Sales is allowed to say
- You may discuss pricing ranges and standard discount bands.
- You must not promise: specific GPU types, fixed latency numbers, or bespoke security features unless already in a signed addendum.

## Checklist (Deal Desk)
- [ ] Deal Intake Form completed
- [ ] Discount band computed and recorded
- [ ] Approvers tagged and approvals recorded
- [ ] Order Form drafted using the latest template
- [ ] If enterprise requires DPA/SLA: open Legal intake per contracting workflow

## FAQ
**Q: Does discount approval mean we can sign?**
A: No. Legal/security/compliance and billing setup steps are separate gates in the end-to-end non-standard enterprise deal process.
